cohort: 2553 women giving birth at a regional rural hospital in KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa
finding: The Robson Ten Group Classification System is a useful tool to identify patient groups (particularly nulliparous women with single cephalic term pregnancies and spontaneous labour) where interventions may be warranted to reduce high caesarean section rates.
mod_finding: The study found a high cesarean section (CS) rate of 42.4%, with nulliparous women experiencing spontaneous labor (Group 1) identified as a key target for interventions to reduce CS rates.
